final_message:
DONE

The workbook is `outputs/Model_I_Headlamp_NPV_Analysis.xlsx`. Vendocrat has the lowest NPV of cost, so I recommend nominating it as lead supplier. Solimoto is the qualified fallback, and Autolantic is not recommended on cost.

The workbook has a Summary sheet, an Inputs & Assumptions sheet and one NPV sheet per vendor. All numbers are live formulas. Excel will calculate them on opening, because I couldn't open the file in a spreadsheet app here. I recalculated it independently with the `formulas` Python package, and it matched my own calculation.

| Vendor | NPV of cost @10% (INR mn) | vs lowest |
|---|---|---|
| Vendocrat | 3,666 | – |
| Solimoto | 3,873 | +5.7% |
| Autolantic | 4,558 | +24.3% |

- **Why Vendocrat wins:** its part prices, tooling and R&D are all the lowest of the three.
- **Gap to the others:** about INR 207 mn NPV against Solimoto and about INR 892 mn against Autolantic.
- **Part price drives the result:** part cost is over 97% of every vendor's total, so the upfront tooling and R&D differences don't change the answer.
- **Ranking holds if Year 1 is also discounted:** I included this as a sensitivity on the Summary sheet.

Assumptions I made that you should confirm (the full list of 12 is on the Inputs & Assumptions sheet):
- **Volumes:** the projected annual volumes are vehicles, and each vehicle takes 2 headlamps.
- **Quoted prices:** I read them as per headlamp, not per set. If they are per set, part costs would be half of those shown, so please confirm with the vendors.
- **Discounting:** I read "10% for years 2, 3, and 4" literally. Year 1 is undiscounted, and Years 2, 3 and 4 are discounted for 1, 2 and 3 periods.
- **Tooling and R&D:** Year 1 volume is exactly 100,000 sets, so all tooling is recovered in Year 1. R&D is paid in Year 1 and split 50/50 between the variants.
- **Solimoto's tiered price:** the higher price applies to the first 100,000 cumulative sets (Year 1), and the lower price applies from set 100,001 onward.
- **Not modelled:** FX, logistics and duties, and technical risk. Autolantic's high FX exposure and 12-week lead time (versus 6 weeks for the Indian vendors) are noted in the comments only.
- **Engineering check:** the recommendation depends on Engineering confirming that Vendocrat can meet the premium LED and dynamic-DRL spec. If it can't, a split award is the next option, but I didn't model it because no per-variant terms were quoted.

The workspace and attachments folders were empty, so the quotations document was the only input.
